key_insight: RPG is a self-improvement framework for embodied agents that boosts robot execution without changing model weights. It reconstructs useful skills from offline data, practices them in simulation, and then transfers that improved behavior to real-world execution.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of building reliable robot manipulation systems across many tasks without requiring constant human effort to annotate rewards, design skills, and manually integrate perception with control.
method: Identify manipulation capabilities from an offline dataset and reconstruct them as reusable practice tasks.
Practice in simulation using execution feedback and privileged signals to improve task performance autonomously.
Deploy the refined execution system on real robots without updating model weights.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path to improving robot performance with less human supervision and lower training cost. For practitioners, it suggests a scalable way to adapt embodied agents to new tasks while avoiding expensive retraining.

paper_title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
paper_authors: Yen-Jen Wang, Haozhe Jiang, Shuying Deng, Haoru Xue, Weirui Ye
